---

I have seen Paul McCartney live 13 times. Porto Alegre, Rio de Janeiro twice in a row, Recife, Montevideo, Porto Alegre again, Buenos Aires, Mexico City, Brasilia, Curitiba, two nights in Sao Paulo, Florianopolis. Fourteen years, four countries, one guy who refuses to slow down.

So I did what I do. I pulled all 13 setlists and counted. Across 85 different songs he played for me over those years, only 12 showed up at every single show. Not once dropped, not once swapped out, across six different tours and a fourteen year gap between the first and the last.

Ob-La-Di, Ob-La-Da is one of the 12. It is my favorite Beatles song, and it turns out Paul agrees with a strange kind of consistency: he has opened himself to plenty of setlist chaos, deep cuts, tour-specific surprises, and this one just never leaves.

Twelve songs is a small, stubborn core inside a much bigger, ever-changing show. I know exactly which one is mine.

Which song would survive all your favorite artist's setlists?
